beats.text: ChatGPT doesn't know what it's going to say next.
Every reply is built one small piece at a time. Those pieces are called tokens.
A token is often a whole word, sometimes just part of one. In English, a token is roughly three quarters of a word.
At every step, the model scores every token it knows, tens of thousands of them, and gives each one a probability.
After "The sky is", "blue" gets a high score. "Banana" gets almost nothing.
It picks one, adds it to the sentence, and does the whole thing again. And again. And again.
A long answer can mean hundreds of these predictions in a few seconds.
So how does it sound so smart? It learned those probabilities from a huge amount of text.
It isn't looking up an answer. It's predicting one, token by token.
That's also why it can sound confident and still be wrong.
